setup: CREATE TABLE t(a INT, k INT); INSERT INTO t VALUES (10, 100); CREATE TABLE t2(p INT, q INT); INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (1, 2); CREATE TABLE n1(id INT, v INT); INSERT INTO n1 VALUES (1,10),(2,20); CREATE TABLE n2(id INT, w INT); INSERT INTO n2 VALUES (1,100),(3,300); CREATE TABLE nc1("ID" INT, a INT); INSERT INTO nc1 VALUES (1,5); CREATE TABLE nc2(id INT, b INT); INSERT INTO nc2 VALUES (1,7); CREATE TABLE x1(a INT); CREATE TABLE x2(b INT); CREATE SCHEMA s1; CREATE TABLE s1.t1(z INT); INSERT INTO s1.t1 VALUES (42); CREATE TABLE tbl(z INT); INSERT INTO tbl VALUES (7);

pins.claim: NULL <op> NULL binder result types: + - * % all bind BIGINT; / binds DOUBLE; = and < bind BOOLEAN; || binds INTEGER (see SQLNULL pin); -NULL binds BIGINT; NOT NULL binds BOOLEAN.
pins.query: DESCRIBE SELECT NULL + NULL AS add_, NULL - NULL AS sub_, NULL * NULL AS mul_, NULL / NULL AS div_, NULL % NULL AS mod_, NULL = NULL AS eq_, NULL < NULL AS lt_, NULL || NULL AS cat_, -NULL AS neg_, NOT NULL AS not_
pins.observed: [('add_', 'BIGINT'), ('sub_', 'BIGINT'), ('mul_', 'BIGINT'), ('div_', 'DOUBLE'), ('mod_', 'BIGINT'), ('eq_', 'BOOLEAN'), ('lt_', 'BOOLEAN'), ('cat_', 'INTEGER'), ('neg_', 'BIGINT'), ('not_', 'BOOLEAN')]

pins.claim: Every NULL <op> NULL VALUE is NULL (never an error) for + - * / % = < ||.
pins.query: SELECT NULL + NULL, NULL - NULL, NULL * NULL, NULL / NULL, NULL % NULL, NULL = NULL, NULL < NULL, NULL || NULL
pins.observed: columns=['(NULL + NULL)', '(NULL - NULL)', '(NULL * NULL)', '(NULL / NULL)', '(NULL % NULL)', '(NULL = NULL)', '(NULL < NULL)', '(NULL || NULL)'] rows=[(None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None)]

pins.claim: typeof cross-check: NULL + NULL genuinely decays to BIGINT and -NULL to BIGINT, but NULL || NULL stays SQLNULL at runtime (typeof returns the string '"NULL"'); NULL = NULL is BOOLEAN.
pins.query: SELECT typeof(NULL + NULL), typeof(NULL || NULL), typeof(NULL = NULL), typeof(-(NULL))
pins.observed: rows=[('BIGINT', '"NULL"', 'BOOLEAN', 'BIGINT')]

pins.claim: Bare NULL (SQLNULL type) is RENDERED as INTEGER by DESCRIBE and materializes as INTEGER in CTAS — this is why DESCRIBE shows NULL || NULL as INTEGER even though typeof says "NULL".
pins.query: DESCRIBE SELECT NULL AS x
pins.observed: [('x', 'INTEGER')]  (also measured: CREATE TABLE ctas_concat AS SELECT NULL || NULL AS x; DESCRIBE ctas_concat -> ('x','INTEGER'); CTAS of NULL + NULL -> ('x','BIGINT'))

pins.claim: SHADOWING KEY PIN: when a select alias collides with a real column, the REAL COLUMN wins for later references. t(a=10,k=100): SELECT a+1 AS k, k*2 gives k=11 but k*2=200 (used column k=100, not alias 11).
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS k, k*2 FROM t

pins.claim: Lateral alias chains work left-to-right: a=10 -> b=11, c=12, d=13.
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS b, b+1 AS c, c+1 AS d FROM t

pins.claim: Select aliases ARE visible in WHERE when no real column has that name: b=a+1=11 matches (complement measured: WHERE b = 10 returns 0 rows).
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS b FROM t WHERE b = 11
pins.observed: columns=['b'] rows=[(11,)]

pins.claim: In WHERE too the real column shadows the alias: WHERE k = 11 (the alias value) matches NOTHING because k resolves to the real column (100).
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS k FROM t WHERE k = 11
pins.observed: columns=['k'] rows=[]

pins.claim: Complement of previous pin: WHERE k = 100 (real column value) DOES match, and the output still shows the alias value 11.
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS k FROM t WHERE k = 100
pins.observed: columns=['k'] rows=[(11,)]

pins.claim: Referencing an alias at an EARLIER select-list position is a binder error (verbatim below). The same error text (with 'c') is produced for an alias referencing a later alias (SELECT c+1 AS b, a+1 AS c FROM t) and for self-reference with no underlying column (SELECT z+1 AS z FROM t).
pins.query: SELECT b*2, a+1 AS b FROM t
pins.observed: BinderException: Binder Error: Column "b" referenced that exists in the SELECT clause - but this column cannot be referenced before it is defined

pins.claim: Self-referencing alias where the column EXISTS uses the real column, no error: SELECT k+1 AS k with k=100 gives 101.
pins.query: SELECT k+1 AS k FROM t
pins.observed: columns=['k'] rows=[(101,)]

pins.claim: An aggregate-result alias IS usable laterally in the same select list: SELECT SUM(a) AS s, s+1 works (10, 11).
pins.query: SELECT SUM(a) AS s, s+1 FROM t

pins.claim: But a select alias is NOT visible inside an aggregate argument: SUM(b) where b is the alias a+1 is a binder error (verbatim below). (Alias in plain GROUP BY works: SELECT a+1 AS b FROM t GROUP BY b -> [(11,)].)
pins.query: SELECT a+1 AS b, SUM(b) FROM t GROUP BY b
pins.observed:
BinderException: Binder Error: Referenced column "b" not found in FROM clause!
Candidate bindings: "a"

LINE 1: SELECT a+1 AS b, SUM(b) FROM t GROUP BY b
                             ^

pins.claim: Column-renaming alias t2 AS u(x, y) works; new names are selectable (SELECT * gives columns ['x','y'] rows [(1,2)]).
pins.query: SELECT x FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
pins.observed: columns=['x'] rows=[(1,)]

pins.claim: PARTIAL rename list is ALLOWED: u(x) on a 2-column table renames only the first column; the rest keep original names -> columns ['x','q'].
pins.query: SELECT * FROM t2 AS u(x)
pins.observed: columns=['x', 'q'] rows=[(1, 2)]

pins.claim: Too many rename names is a binder error (verbatim below).
pins.query: SELECT * FROM t2 AS u(x, y, z)
pins.observed: BinderException: Binder Error: table "t2" has 2 columns available but 3 columns specified

pins.claim: Renamed names shadow originals ENTIRELY: the old bare column name p is no longer addressable; error suggests the new name.
pins.query: SELECT p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
pins.observed:
BinderException: Binder Error: Referenced column "p" not found in FROM clause!
Candidate bindings: "x"

LINE 1: SELECT p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
               ^

pins.claim: Qualified old name u.p also fails, with a DIFFERENT error shape ('Table "u" does not have a column named ...' listing both new names).
pins.query: SELECT u.p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
pins.observed:
BinderException: Binder Error: Table "u" does not have a column named "p"

Candidate bindings: : "x", "y"

LINE 1: SELECT u.p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
               ^

pins.claim: The original table name is dead as a qualifier once aliased: t2.p errors with 'Referenced table "t2" not found! Candidate tables: "u"'. (u.x works: [(1,)].)
pins.query: SELECT t2.p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
pins.observed:
BinderException: Binder Error: Referenced table "t2" not found!
Candidate tables: "u"

LINE 1: SELECT t2.p FROM t2 AS u(x, y)
               ^

pins.claim: NATURAL JOIN dedups the matched column like USING: n1(id,v) NATURAL JOIN n2(id,w) outputs 3 columns in order [id, v, w] (join column first, then left rest, then right rest); only id=1 matches. DESCRIBE types: id INTEGER, v INTEGER, w INTEGER.
pins.query: SELECT * FROM n1 NATURAL JOIN n2

pins.claim: Despite dedup in *, BOTH sides' join columns remain addressable qualified: n1.id and n2.id both bind.
pins.query: SELECT n1.id, n2.id FROM n1 NATURAL JOIN n2
pins.observed: columns=['id', 'id'] rows=[(1, 1)]

pins.claim: Case-differing column names DO match in NATURAL JOIN (identifier matching is case-insensitive): nc1("ID",a) NATURAL JOIN nc2(id,b) joins on ID/id; output uses the LEFT table's spelling 'ID'.
pins.query: SELECT * FROM nc1 NATURAL JOIN nc2
pins.observed: columns=['ID', 'a', 'b'] rows=[(1, 5, 7)]

pins.claim: NATURAL JOIN with NO common columns is a hard binder ERROR, not a cross product (verbatim below).
pins.query: SELECT * FROM x1 NATURAL JOIN x2
pins.observed:
BinderException: Binder Error: No columns found to join on in NATURAL JOIN.
Use CROSS JOIN if you intended for this to be a cross-product.
   Left candidates: x1.a
   Right candidates: x2.b

LINE 1: SELECT * FROM x1 NATURAL JOIN x2
                         ^

pins.claim: NATURAL LEFT JOIN: unmatched left rows keep the left id value and NULL-fill the right-only columns: id=2 -> (2, 20, NULL).
pins.query: SELECT * FROM n1 NATURAL LEFT JOIN n2 ORDER BY id

pins.claim: Schema-qualified access works: SELECT * FROM s1.t1 -> [(42,)]. Explicit main.tbl also works -> [(7,)].
pins.query: SELECT * FROM s1.t1
pins.observed: columns=['z'] rows=[(42,)]

pins.claim: Bare name does NOT search other schemas: SELECT * FROM t1 when only s1.t1 exists is a Catalog Error with a did-you-mean suggestion (verbatim below).
pins.query: SELECT * FROM t1
pins.observed:
CatalogException: Catalog Error: Table with name t1 does not exist!
Did you mean "s1.t1"?

LINE 1: SELECT * FROM t1
                      ^

pins.claim: Unknown schema qualifier does NOT fall back to bare-name lookup: SELECT * FROM test.tbl when only main.tbl exists errors on the missing SCHEMA (verbatim below); same shape for fully-nonexistent nosuch.nothing.
pins.query: SELECT * FROM test.tbl
pins.observed:
CatalogException: Catalog Error: Table with name "test.tbl" does not exist because schema "test" does not exist.

LINE 1: SELECT * FROM test.tbl
                      ^

pins.claim: 1 IN ('1', 2) -> True; the string is cast to the numeric side (result type BOOLEAN via DESCRIBE). Also True for -1 IN ('-1', 2) and 1 IN ('01', 2) (numeric, not lexicographic).
pins.query: SELECT 1 IN ('1', 2)
pins.observed: rows=[(True,)]

pins.claim: 1 IN ('abc') raises a bind-time Conversion Error (verbatim below).
pins.query: SELECT 1 IN ('abc')
pins.observed:
ConversionException: Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'abc' to INT32

LINE 1: SELECT 1 IN ('abc')
                     ^

pins.claim: 'a' BETWEEN 1 AND 2 raises Conversion Error (verbatim below). Same error family for 'héllo' = 1, 'a😀b' = 1, '' = 1, and 'inf' = 1 — each says "Could not convert string '<s>' to INT32".
pins.query: SELECT 'a' BETWEEN 1 AND 2
pins.observed:
ConversionException: Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'a' to INT32

LINE 1: SELECT 'a' BETWEEN 1 AND 2
               ^

pins.claim: '5' BETWEEN 1 AND 10 -> True (string cast to numeric side).
pins.query: SELECT '5' BETWEEN 1 AND 10
pins.observed: rows=[(True,)]

pins.claim: Comparison is NUMERIC, not lexicographic: '10' BETWEEN 2 AND 20 -> True (lexicographic '10' < '2' would give False). '5.5' BETWEEN 1 AND 10 -> True; '  5  ' = 5 -> True (whitespace trimmed); '1e2' = 100 -> True.
pins.query: SELECT '10' BETWEEN 2 AND 20
pins.observed: rows=[(True,)]

pins.claim: TRUE IN (1, 0) -> True. Direction: the BOOLEAN is compared as 1 — TRUE = 1 -> True, TRUE = 2 -> False, TRUE IN (2, 0) -> False — even though CAST(2 AS BOOLEAN) is True, so the ints are NOT cast to BOOLEAN.
pins.query: SELECT TRUE IN (1, 0)
pins.observed: rows=[(True,)]  (also measured: SELECT TRUE = 2 -> [(False,)]; SELECT TRUE IN (2, 0) -> [(False,)]; SELECT CAST(2 AS BOOLEAN) -> [(True,)])

pins.claim: 1 = '1' -> True. 1 = 'abc' raises Conversion Error (verbatim below), identical text to the IN case.
pins.query: SELECT 1 = 'abc'
pins.observed:
ConversionException: Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'abc' to INT32

LINE 1: SELECT 1 = 'abc'
                   ^

pins.claim: Decimal strings compared to ints are cast with ROUNDING (half away from zero), not error and not truncation: 2 = '1.5' -> True, 1 = '1.5' -> False, 1 = '1.0' -> True, 1 IN ('1.5', 2) -> False. CAST('1.5' AS INTEGER)=2, CAST('2.5')=3, CAST('-1.5')=-2, CAST('0.5')=1, CAST('-2.5')=-3.
pins.query: SELECT 2 = '1.5'
pins.observed: rows=[(True,)]  (also measured: SELECT 1 = '1.5' -> [(False,)]; SELECT CAST('1.5' AS INTEGER), CAST('2.5' AS INTEGER), CAST('-1.5' AS INTEGER), CAST('0.5' AS INTEGER), CAST('-2.5' AS INTEGER) -> [(2, 3, -2, 1, -3)])

pins.claim: Standard 3-valued IN with NULL: 2 IN (NULL, 1) -> NULL, but 1 IN (NULL, 1) -> True; 5 BETWEEN NULL AND 10 -> NULL.
pins.query: SELECT 2 IN (NULL, 1)
pins.observed: rows=[(None,)]  (also measured: SELECT 1 IN (NULL, 1) -> [(True,)]; SELECT 5 BETWEEN NULL AND 10 -> [(None,)])

pins.claim: Boundary ints: 2147483648 = '2147483648' -> True (unifies at BIGINT); 9223372036854775807 = '9223372036854775807' -> True; but '9223372036854775808' = 9223372036854775807 raises "Conversion Error: Could not convert string '9223372036854775808' to INT64" — no fallback to wider type.
pins.observed:
ConversionException: Conversion Error: Could not convert string '9223372036854775808' to INT64

LINE 1: SELECT '9223372036854775808' = 9223372036854775807
               ^

pins.claim: try_trim_null does NOT exist in DuckDB 1.5.5 (verbatim error below).
pins.query: SELECT try_trim_null('x')
pins.observed:
CatalogException: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name try_trim_null does not exist!
Did you mean "try_strptime"?

               ^

pins.claim: COLUMNS is NOT a scalar function: SELECT COLUMNS('x') without FROM errors as a star expression (verbatim below).
pins.query: SELECT COLUMNS('x')
pins.observed: BinderException: Binder Error: * expression without FROM clause!

pins.claim: With a FROM clause COLUMNS('regex') is a star-like expansion matching column names by regex: on t(a,k), COLUMNS('a') expands to just column a; COLUMNS('.*') expands to [a, k]; COLUMNS('k') to [k].
pins.query: SELECT COLUMNS('a') FROM t
pins.observed: columns=['a'] rows=[(10,)]  (also measured: SELECT COLUMNS('.*') FROM t -> columns=['a','k'] rows=[(10,100)]; SELECT COLUMNS('k') FROM t -> columns=['k'] rows=[(100,)])

surprises: Lateral alias shadowing goes the OPPOSITE way from what many engines do: the real column beats the select alias, in both the select list (k*2 used column k=100 -> 200) and WHERE (WHERE k=11 matched nothing).
WHERE can reference select-list aliases at all (non-standard SQL), but only when no real column of that name exists.

NULL || NULL does NOT decay like arithmetic: typeof is SQLNULL ('"NULL"') while NULL + NULL is genuinely BIGINT and NULL / NULL genuinely DOUBLE; DESCRIBE/CTAS render SQLNULL as INTEGER (same as bare SELECT NULL).
VARCHAR-vs-INT comparison casts the string to the integer and ROUNDS half-away-from-zero: 2 = '1.5' is TRUE and 1 = '1.5' is FALSE — no error, no truncation, no DOUBLE fallback.
BOOLEAN-vs-INT comparison casts the BOOLEAN to the integer (TRUE=1 true, TRUE=2 false) even though CAST(2 AS BOOLEAN) is true — direction matters.
NATURAL JOIN with no common columns is a hard Binder Error, NOT a cross product.
Case-differing column names ("ID" vs id) DO natural-join; output takes the left table's spelling.
Partial rename alias u(x) on a 2-column table is legal and renames only a prefix of the columns.
An aggregate alias is laterally usable (SUM(a) AS s, s+1) but aliases are invisible inside aggregate ARGUMENTS (SUM(b) errors); plain GROUP BY b (alias) works.
Unknown schema qualifier fails on the schema, with no fallback to bare-name lookup: test.tbl errors even though tbl exists in main.
recommendation: For schema-qualified names our engine (which registers row tables by BARE name) should mirror DuckDB: accept 'main.tbl' as an alias for bare 'tbl' (DuckDB resolves main.tbl; measured [(7,)]), and REJECT any other qualifier with an error matching DuckDB's shape: 'Catalog Error: Table with name "test.tbl" does not exist because schema "test" does not exist.' Do NOT silently resolve test.tbl to bare tbl. For binder semantics: implement real-column-wins alias shadowing in SELECT and WHERE, left-to-right alias chains, the exact 'cannot be referenced before it is defined' error for forward/earlier references, USING-style dedup + qualified-both-sides addressability for NATURAL JOIN, hard error on NATURAL JOIN with no common columns, string->int comparison casts with half-away-from-zero rounding and verbatim 'Could not convert string ... to INT32/INT64' Conversion Errors, and BOOLEAN->INT (not INT->BOOLEAN) direction for bool/int comparisons.
